narration.en: Price is the only P that brings in money. Cost, demand, competition and law all pull it in different directions.

body.en: Price is the amount of money paid by buyers in exchange for a product or service. Factors affecting price: product cost (fixed, variable and semi-variable costs set the lower limit), utility and demand (the upper limit is what buyers are willing to pay), extent of competition, government and legal regulations, pricing objectives (profit maximisation, market share, facing competition, product quality leadership), and the marketing methods used.
body.kn: ಬೆಲೆ ಎಂದರೆ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನದ ವಿನಿಮಯಕ್ಕೆ ಖರೀದಿದಾರ ಕೊಡುವ ಹಣ. ಉತ್ಪನ್ನದ ವೆಚ್ಚ, ಉಪಯುಕ್ತತೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬೇಡಿಕೆ, ಸ್ಪರ್ಧೆ, ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ನಿಯಮಗಳು, ಬೆಲೆ ಉದ್ದೇಶಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಮಾರಾಟ ವಿಧಾನಗಳು ಬೆಲೆಯ ಮೇಲೆ ಪ್ರಭಾವ ಬೀರುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: Price lies between a floor and a ceiling.
Cost sets the floor; what buyers will pay sets the ceiling; competition decides where in between.
Law and the firm's objectives, such as market share, also shape the price.
Bottles: fixed cost 2 lakh, variable cost 30, price 50. Contribution is 20 per bottle.
On a graph, total revenue starts at zero, total cost starts at the fixed cost. They cross at 10,000 bottles.

text.en: Break-even sales: {bep:1} thousand units a month
Price below variable cost: every sale adds to the loss

body.en: In the long run, price must cover the total cost. The volume at which total revenue equals total cost is the break-even point: $\text{BEP} = \frac{\text{Fixed cost}}{\text{Price} - \text{Variable cost per unit}}$. A higher price lowers the break-even volume but may reduce demand.
body.kn: ದೀರ್ಘಾವಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬೆಲೆ ಒಟ್ಟು ವೆಚ್ಚವನ್ನು ಭರಿಸಬೇಕು. ಒಟ್ಟು ಆದಾಯ ಒಟ್ಟು ವೆಚ್ಚಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮವಾಗುವ ಮಾರಾಟ ಪ್ರಮಾಣವೇ ಸಮತೋಲನ ಬಿಂದು.

narration.en: In the long run, price must cover the total cost. The volume at which total revenue equals total cost is the break-even point: fixed cost divided by price minus variable cost per unit. A higher price lowers the break-even volume, but may reduce demand.

aim.en: To see how the selling price changes the break-even point: the sales volume at which total revenue just covers total cost.

narration.en: Let us open the break-even bench. Change the selling price and watch how many units we must sell before we start making a profit.

caption.en: Total revenue and total cost against sales (thousand units). Where the lines cross is the break-even point.

narration.en: Change the price and the costs and watch where total revenue overtakes total cost.

tryThis.en: Default values: check 10,000 bottles at ₹50. Then raise the price to ₹70.
Raise the fixed cost. Which line moves, and where does the crossing go?
Make the variable cost close to the price. Why does break-even shoot up?

problem.en: A firm making steel water bottles has fixed costs of ₹2,00,000 a year and a variable cost of ₹30 per bottle. How many bottles must it sell to break even at a price of ₹50? At ₹70?

steps.en: At ₹50: contribution per bottle = 50 − 30 = ₹20; BEP = 2,00,000 ÷ 20 = 10,000 bottles.
A higher price halves the break-even volume, but demand at ₹70 may be lower: cost and demand must both be considered.
